sourceUnitAudit.jobHours: weeklyHoursOf(role) returns the role weekly-range midpoint. population586 and opening-employment509 divide by central daysPerWeek into a calendar-day average.
sourceUnitAudit.fallbackSlots: openingWorkCommitments74 multiplies by daysPerWeek and minutesPerHour, then multiplies periodDays/daysPerWeek and divides by configured slot count. Sum per period conserves the role weekly hours.
sourceUnitAudit.canonicalSlots: opening-work copies workSchedulesFor.shift.minutes for each worksOn date across the full declared period. Supplied slots override fallback minutes.
sourceUnitAudit.hourlyPay: Actual requested cents follow stored hourlyMinor times attendedMinutes/minutesPerHour, with carried fractional minor units; wageDailyMinor is not used as a weekday shift payment.

blockers: Compact receipt does not contain openingAllocation age/role targets, job-hours/status histogram, per-age planned minutes, or feasibility-only refusals.
Added workers copy their template person's part-time hours and complete timetable; observed full/part-time distribution and roster staggering are absent.
Legacy townResidents filters to ages18-66, while reference rows include employed16-17 and67+; no actual retirement/legal-minor eligibility producer resolves that mismatch.
Only21 supported ordinary occupations are expandable; public/institutional and other unsupported source mass stays unfilled.
No observed employer headcount/capacity, sourced position funding, within-role hours dispersion, real holiday/leave/on-call calendar or complete daily diary.
Primary-job-only commitment contract excludes multiple-job accounting.
Current closed money lacks employer customer transactions, household bill transfers, borrowing/revenue/closure; unpaid fraction alone cannot prove any payroll-to-attendance causal response.
recommendation: Diagnose coverage and template schedule mix first. No hours/attendance coefficient scaling or unit multiplier is justified. Any new numeric data rows need central tagged metadata and honest blocked calibration references.
